(1) the Totoltepc pluton is the product of an early Permian continental arc that developed along the western margin Pangea-A, (2) the Totoltec and Tecomate formations are the product of the same arc, and (3), the Tecomate formation was deposited in a forearc basin.

(1) arc magmatism in southern Mexico was initiated in the late Paleozoic, (2) the arc was active for ~17 m.y. (306–289 Ma) and was followed by ~30 m.y. of quiescence (ca. 289–260 Ma), and (3) arc magmatismo and basin evolution were contemporaneous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the late Paleozoic evolution of the arc and back-arc basin along the western margin and periphery of Pangaean North America.
the evolution of an active continental margin that developed along the western margin during the amalgamation of the supercontinent Pangea.
the development and evolution of a late Paleozoicoceanic arc system in a continental margin setting, which was active during the amalgamation and breakup stages of supercontinent formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Totoltepecton-Tecomate assemblage represents a postcollisional arc system that developed in response to the subduction of the Pacific oceanic lithosphere along the western margin Pangea.
the Totoltepecton and Tecomate Formation are products of a late Paleozoice arc system, which is consistent with subduction of the Pacific plate beneath Pangea.
the arc magmatism of the Totoltepce pluton and the Tecomate basin fill are the result of the subduction of the Farallon plate beneath the western margin Pangea-A, during the late Paleozoic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

arc-related igneous activity and sedimentation in the Acatlan region of southern Mexico are coeval with the amalgamation of the Pangea supercontinent and that the arc was located in a less mature part of the arc than the arc to the south.
the Acatlan complex represents a late Paleozoicoceanic arc and forearc basin that developed on the margin of a Pangaean continent.
the Totoltepex and Tecomate assemblage represents a continental arc developed along the western margin (Pacific Ocean) of the Pangea-A continent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Acatlan arc and basin were developed in a peripheral position to the Pangean supercontinent, but the timing of the arc and basin formation relative to Pangea amalgamation and breakup remains uncertain.
the Acatlan arc was active during the late Paleozoic and was a source of detrital zircon for the Tecomate strata.

the Totoltepc pluton and Tecomate Formation were deposited in the same tectonic setting, which is consistent with a late Paleozoicrogenic event along the western margin, or paleo-Pacific side, of Pangea.
